newsitem.title: JAPAN: DOLLAR SEEN SOFTER VS YEN IN ASIA.
newsitem.headline: DOLLAR SEEN SOFTER VS YEN IN ASIA.

text.p: The dollar is likely to be softer against the yen in Asia on Thursday following its overnight fall, particularly against the mark, dealers said.
"It is not surprising if the dollar dips below 115 yen," said a senior dealer at a Japanese trust bank.
If the dollar falls below New York's low of around 115.25 yen, it may briefly reach around 114.80 yen, he said.

He said Japanese investors' buying is expected to emerge on falls, but their buying energy may recede after recent heavy buying. The dollar's recovery could be slow and its topside would be limited at around 116.00 yen, he added.
A Japanese bank dealer said the dollar was likely to be supported at the lower end of 115-116 yen, but if the dollar breaks through 114.50 yen that could open the way for a further downward trend.
But she said the market could lack such energy in the midst of the Japanese summer holiday season.
The trust bank dealer said mark buying against the yen may provide support to dollar/yen rate indirectly.
The mark, which has succumbed to heavy selling pressure against the yen, was set to rise slowly after it broke through 62.60 yen on Wednesday, dealers said .

Overnight, the dollar was hurt by expectations of higher German interest rates and a report suggesting Europe's single currency might be postponed. The Bundesbank also warned of rising consumer prices and said it would gear monetary policy towards keeping inflation under control.
The mark was also bought against sterling, which also helped push the dollar down against the mark, dealers said.

The trust bank dealer said he would also closely watch the U.S. stock market. "If the current corrective phase in the stock market prolongs, investments in dollar assets will not revive and will limit the dollar's rise," he added.
